hints.body: Start with only A in the queue. Row 1 is what happens when A leaves.
For each row: take the vertex at the front of the queue, add it to the order, then add its neighbours that haven't been found yet, in alphabetical order, at the back.
Row 1: A leaves, and B and C join. Row 2: B leaves, and only D is new.
Answer: the order is A, B, C, D. The queue after each row is [B, C], [C, D], [D], []. At row 3, D is not added again because it is already waiting in the queue.
